A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PLLB work. All 21 pages of v2 and 26 pages of v3, including appendices, are readable, and corresponding text, equations, figures, and tables can be matched despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on SaySelect, Maze, Builder, Birds, and robot grasping, together with three human-subject studies.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and human studies and adds quantitative sensitivity tests and non-contrastive ablations in Appendices B.10–B.11.

M1.justification: The proposed contrastive rule-generation loop, rule-guided policy updates, model components, and robot controller remain unchanged. Expanded explanations of policy conditioning and the new experimental ablations do not revise the proposed PLLB procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same five tasks, bird-image coverage, maze transfer scenarios, robot environments, and human-study populations. The added appendix experiments vary rule generation within existing task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds a high-reward-only, non-contrastive comparator in SaySelect and Birds (Tables 8–9), alongside prompt-variant controls in Tables 6–7. The comparator sets in the retained main experiments are unchanged.

E3.justification: The new analyses introduce three alternative prompts, sampling temperatures of 0.1 and 0.9 around the default 0.5, and high-reward-only example selection. Existing main-experiment metrics, training budgets, and splits remain unchanged; the clearer grasp-transfer initialization description is additional disclosure.

E4.justification: Appendices B.10–B.11 add systematic prompt and temperature sensitivity tests in SaySelect and directly test the contribution of negative examples in SaySelect and Birds. These substantially extend the previous adversarial-rule, transfer, and qualitative model-comparison analyses by testing central rule-generation choices.

E5.justification: Tables 6–9 specify five-trial averages with ± values, although the uncertainty measure is not defined. Section 7.3 omits v2's Bonferroni-correction qualifier for the Builder Wilcoxon test. The retained grasp experiments still report 20 random seeds; no increase in their run count is established.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial quantitative findings on sensitivity and contrastive example selection while retaining the main plotted outcomes. In Table 8, original versus non-contrastive SaySelect results at 6,000 episodes are 0.96 versus 0.91 reward and 0.97 versus 0.88 interpretability. Table 9 adds Birds comparisons, including background rewards of 2.30 versus 1.78.

T1.justification: The MDP formulation, Q-learning regularizer, and reward definitions are retained. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs, and v3's added conceptual explanations introduce no new mathematical results.

C1.justification: v3 explicitly qualifies generalization as few-shot transfer in the introduction and Sections 6.1 and 8.3. Section 4 also adds a first-to-validate claim about self-generated LM rules for training human participants. The central performance, interpretability, and human-coordination contributions remain.

C2.justification: Section 9 substantially expands discussion of non-linguistic abstractions, false trust in generated rules, stochastic rewards, reward misspecification, and action-space limitations. Appendix B.11 adds an explanation that negative examples help exclude spurious caption features. These extend v2's narrower discussion of trajectory representations and overly abstract rules.

D1.justification: v3 newly discloses the default SaySelect sampling temperature and full sensitivity-test prompts. Section 8.3 explicitly describes initializing grasp-transfer evaluations from learned policies and continuing environment updates. Existing hyperparameters, main prompts, and source-code access information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds the human-training validation novelty claim and discusses positioning against non-linguistic bottlenecks. It removes the ten Pas et al. (2017) grasping citation and reference. The principal related-work coverage and comparisons with language-based agents remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 edits the abstract and introductory prose, expands method explanations, clarifies generalization terminology, and regroups appendix material under Appendix B. Much existing wording and the main scientific section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column formatting to a single-column journal layout. Figures 1–2 are revised, learning-curve panels are rearranged, and v2 Figures 8–10 are consolidated into v3 Figure 6. The task overview and reconstruction examples move to the appendix, and four new quantitative tables are added.

improvement.justification: The new non-contrastive ablations directly test the value of negative examples, while prompt and temperature checks strengthen validation of rule generation. Clearer few-shot transfer descriptions and expanded limitations improve interpretation of the evidence. These provide a modest overall gain, tempered by undefined ± statistics and the lost Builder Bonferroni-correction qualifier.
